interest: Laurel III's academy bid and barred inspection of Taiwan manganese.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.22711B) documents U.S. State Department oversight of Philippine nationals seeking access to Japanese military institutions and strategic industrial facilities during the 1930s. The first portion of the file (April–June 1935) centers on Jose Sotero Laurel III, son of prominent Philippine statesman Jose P. Laurel, who sought U.S. diplomatic intercession to gain admission to the Imperial Military Academy in Tokyo after failing to obtain a West Point appointment; following consultations with the War Department, the State Department formally instructed Ambassador Joseph C. Grew not to sponsor Laurel. The second portion of the file (February–March 1939) comprises confidential despatches and comprehensive memoranda from American Consul Gerald Warner in Taihoku, Taiwan, regarding Sotero Escarrilla, a representative of the Negros Mining Company of Manila. Escarrilla traveled to Taiwan at the invitation of Taiwan Denka Kaisha to arbitrate a commercial dispute over a shipment of manganese ore, but was repeatedly blocked by Japanese military authorities from inspecting processing plants in the fortified zones of Keelung and Rato, subjected to daily police interrogations, and saddled with exorbitant labor and currency charges.

subfiles.about: A confidential consular memorandum detailing Escarrilla's inspection mission, military entry refusals, police surveillance, and commercial exploitation in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: Consul Gerald Warner provides an exhaustive chronological account of Sotero Escarrilla's attempt to inspect manganese facilities in Keelung and Rato operated by Taiwan Denka Kaisha. Despite personal appeals by consular staff to Taiwan Commander-in-Chief Lieutenant-General Kodama and local fortress commander Captain Yamahashi, military authorities consistently denied factory entry citing fortress zone regulations. Escarrilla endured daily two-hour police interrogations, inflated labor and interpreter bills, disadvantageous exchange rates, and duplicitous behavior by company manager Kobayashi, illustrating the severe obstacles facing foreign traders in wartime Japan.
subfiles.title: Confidential Memorandum by Gerald Warner regarding Sotero Escarrilla in Taiwan

subfiles.summary: Copy of Warner's despatch No. 65 for the Philippine Government.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Despatch No. 65 from Gerald Warner to Secretary of State

subfiles.about: An extra certified copy of the confidential memorandum detailing Escarrilla's surveillance, military obstruction, and commercial dispute in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: This is a certified true copy of Consul Gerald Warner's confidential memorandum dated February 28, 1939 (with addenda from March 7 and 15, 1939). It recounts Escarrilla's dealings with Taiwan Denka Kaisha, intervention by the American Consulate with military commanders Kodama and Yamahashi, daily police interrogations in Keelung, and exorbitant sorting fees. The memorandum concludes with wage statistics from the Japan Advertiser demonstrating the artificial inflation of labor costs charged to the Filipino firm.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Confidential Memorandum by Gerald Warner regarding Sotero Escarrilla
